The async function `stopGpsAndSwitchToOD` lacks proper error handling. If `stopGpsTrip()` fails (e.g., location API error, Onyx error), the modal will be closed but the GPS tracking may still be active, leaving the app in an inconsistent state. Additionally, if the component unmounts during execution, there is no cleanup or cancellation mechanism.

Suggested fix: Wrap the operations in a try-catch block and handle errors appropriately. Either re-open the modal on error or show an error message to the user.

The span CONST.TELEMETRY.SPAN_BOOTSPLASH.LOCALE is ended here, but it is also ended in LocaleContextProvider.tsx line 134 when areTranslationsLoading becomes false. This creates a race condition where endSpan may be called twice on the same span, or called in the wrong order. The first endSpan to execute will properly close the span, but the second will attempt to end an already-closed span, potentially causing telemetry errors.

**Suggested fix:** Remove the endSpan from LocaleContextProvider.tsx since this new implementation in Expensify.tsx correctly ends the span when preferredLocale is available, or add logic to ensure endSpan is only called once.

The span CONST.TELEMETRY.SPAN_BOOTSPLASH.PUBLIC_ROOM_API is started on line 276 inside the if (reportID && !isAuthenticated) condition, but it is ended unconditionally in doneCheckingPublicRoom() which is called from multiple code paths including the else branch (line 283) where the span was never started. This creates a span lifecycle issue where endSpan is called without a corresponding startSpan, potentially causing telemetry errors.

**Suggested fix:** Only call endSpan when the span was actually started. Move endSpan out of doneCheckingPublicRoom() and call it explicitly only in the code paths where startSpan was called.
